ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) and the Grand-Ducal Regulations of 18 February 2019 and 17 August 2020; Law of 8 May 2023 restricting public RBE access implementing CJEU C-37/20 and C-601/20; Law of 19 December 2016 on the RCS/LBR; Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended, introducing the SCSp by the Law of 12 July 2013 (Article 102-1 et seq.); CSSF Regulation 12-02 and CSSF Circular 18/698; EU Regulation 2023/1113 and the EU/UN/OFAC sanctions framework.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille not required for domestic formation; the deed is registered electronically with LBR using authenticated signatures, and the notarial original remains with the notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing of the corporate General Partner, if constituted outside Luxembourg
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign companies registry in the General Partner's country of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney (procuration) granted to the Luxembourg filing agent, counsel or domiciliation provider for RCS, RBE and registered office formalities
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or equivalent competent authority in the grantor's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization for non-Hague jurisdictions, followed by sworn translation into French or German

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Judicial or criminal records authority of each partner's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization for non-Hague jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies and proof of residential address (CDD/KYC evidence) of all UBOs and authorized signatories

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all General Partners, UBOs, authorized representatives and material counterparties against the UN Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, OFAC SDN and Non-SDN lists, UK HMT sanctions, and domestic Luxembourg sanctions measures, together with PEP database checks (World-Check, Dow Jones or equivalent), prior to RBE filing and bank onboarding; ongoing transaction monitoring is required under the Law of 12 November 2004, as amended, and CSSF Circular 18/698. The business is classified Low_Risk_Standard for an unregulated ISIC 6201 remote-screen-share / IoT telemetry software activity, but the SCSp remains subject to full customer due diligence, source-of-funds verification, and reporting to the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (CRF) upon any suspicious activity.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) e-filing portal at www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be registered in Latin script in any language provided they are distinctive and consistent with public order; all constitutive filings in a non-official language must be accompanied by a sworn translation into French or German. An SCSp corporate name must include the legal-form designation 'Société en Commandite Spéciale' or the acronym 'SCSp' as a prefix or suffix, and the name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing RCS-registered name or protected trademark.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant may obtain the written grounds from LBR and file a 'recours gracieux' (administrative appeal) with the competent coordinating ministry, namely the Ministry of Justice or the Ministry of the Economy, within three months, followed by a 'recours contentieux' before the Administrative Tribunal of Luxembourg if the administrative appeal is denied. The applicant may simultaneously re-submit a distinct alternative name through the LBR portal; an expiring reservation must be renewed before its end date and is subject to LBR administrative practice on extension. A rejected name may not be reserved pending appeal unless reinstated by the competent authority.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted only through a licensed societe de domiciliation authorized under the Law of 31 May 1999, which must hold Ministry of the Economy authorization and provide a verifiable physical Luxembourg address. A genuine registered office in Luxembourg is compulsory for RCS and RBE registration; pure online mail-forwarding virtual addresses or shared mailboxes without a licensed domiciliation agent are not acceptable for an SCSp in this software/IoT business segment.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low, estimated at less than 10% annual probability for an unregulated remote-screen-share and IoT telemetry software SCSp. Unannounced on-site inspection is not a standard RCS or RBE supervisory tool; the primary triggers are inconsistency between the RBE declaration, bank onboarding files and economic substance records, or an active AML/CRF inquiry during payment-provider onboarding with Stripe or Paddle, or during Luxembourg corporate income tax and VAT audits.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, Articles 13-1 to 13-9 (Société en Commandite Spéciale / SCSp)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: RCS registration declaration and publication in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an SCSp; capital contributions are freely determined in the partnership agreement and no escrow or blocked capital account is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the undersigned partners of LU_SCSP, having reviewed the draft partnership agreement, hereby approve the subscription of partnership interests as set out in the subscription schedule, with no statutory minimum capital contribution and no escrow requirement. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the partnership be established at [address] in Luxembourg City, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg. RESOLVED, that [Name] be and is hereby appointed as general manager(s) (gérant(s)) of the partnership, with sole authority to execute filings, open bank accounts, and register the partnership with the Luxembourg Business Registers and all tax authorities. RESOLVED, that the gérant(s) be authorised to take all necessary steps to obtain tax identification numbers, VAT registration, and platform payment accounts, and to sign all regulatory filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS online name search portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search on the LBR/RCS portal for the proposed partnership name. File a formal name reservation application if available, or proceed directly to partnership agreement drafting once confirmation of availability is obtained.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or conflicts with an existing registered name, submit an alternative name or appeal the objection through the RCS regularisation procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the SCSp Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: External Luxembourg counsel or notarial office (optional notarisation; private deed permitted)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the partnership agreement (contrat de société) identifying the general partner(s), limited partner(s), capital contributions, profit-sharing arrangements, management powers, duration, and Luxembourg registered office address. Execute the agreement in the required form, with all partners signing personally and signatures legalised where required.
required_dossiers: Proof of physical address or registered office letter from landlord
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry or notary queries the permitting of a partner or UBO, amend the agreement or submit supplementary identification and source-of-funds documentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Subscription of Partnership Interests and Initial Contribution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General partner (gérant) and, if capital is contributed, a Luxembourg bank account
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the agreed capital contributions as set out in the partnership agreement. If a capital contribution is made, open a bank account in the name of the SCSp and deposit the contribution; otherwise, record that no contribution has been paid and that no escrow requirement applies.
required_dossiers: Subscription schedule listing partners and amounts
Bank deposit certificate, if capital contributed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If banking counterparty requests additional corporate documents, provide the executed partnership agreement and the forthcoming RCS registration reference; no statutory cure is required for delay.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Partners and designated gérant(s) of the SCSp
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold a formal decision meeting of the partners and adopt a written first resolution approving the subscription schedule, adopting the Luxembourg registered office, appointing the gérant(s), and authorising the gérant(s) to sign all incorporation filings, open bank accounts, and instruct professional advisers.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry requires a notarised form because of subsequent legal authentication, have the resolution executed before a Luxembourg notary and refile within the prescribed cure period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS electronic filing desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the registration dossier with the RCS within one month of execution of the partnership agreement. Include the signed partnership agreement, first managers resolution, identification of all partners and managers, UBO declarations, registered office consent, and proof of payment of the filing fee. Upon registration the RCS issues the registration number; the registry publishes a notice in the RESA.
required_dossiers: Identification documents of partners and managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a regularisation request, file the missing documents or corrections in accordance with the registry notice within the specified cure period; administrative appeal is available if registration is refused.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS) if employees are hired
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register with the ACD and AEDT for the fiscal identification number and, if taxable under Luxembourg VAT rules, submit the VAT registration form. For remote software services with Stripe/Paddle payment rails, obtain VAT number and business identification codes. Register with the CCSS only when engaging local employees.
required_dossiers: Description of remote software and telemetry services
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax authorities query the VAT registration, provide the commercial contracts, platform description, and target market analysis showing any applicable reverse-charge or VAT remittance requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – no industry-specific operating licence is required for ISIC 6201 / NAICS 511210 remote desktop software and telemetry services under Luxembourg law.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial operating permit or sectoral licence applies to a purely digital remote screen-share and IoT telemetry service company.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – purely digital service with no physical installation, wastewater discharge, atmospheric emissions, or hazardous-waste generation
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable; if a standard office premises is used, comply with municipal waste handling rules and EU energy performance of buildings requirements for office HVAC and IT equipment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No civil-defence or structural-load clearance applies to remote software operations. For any leased office, obtain the municipal fire-safety certificate for ordinary office occupancy and comply with the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM) workplace health and safety standards for employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) — Registration Duties, Estates and VAT Authority, L-2946 Luxembourg (portal: myguichet.lu / AEDT e-space); direct income tax: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: SCSp is registered at the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR/RCS) to obtain the national business number (matricule) filed by the general partner; Luxembourg VAT ID (LU + 8 digits) is obtained by filing VAT registration Form 640 with the AEDT before commencing taxable activity. Non-EU-established taxable persons must appoint an AEDT-approved tax representative in Luxembourg; EU-established persons may register directly. The SCSp as a fiscal-transparent vehicle has no separate direct-tax TIN and partners are identified by their domestic TINs.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The SCSp is mandatorily fiscally transparent (no CIT, net wealth tax or municipal business tax at entity level); partners are taxed directly and the partnership agreement determines profit attribution. No check-the-box election exists in Luxembourg law. For VAT: the SCSp may elect to be treated as a taxable person when exercising an economic activity, may join an 'assujetti unique' VAT group, or benefit from the small-business franchise (turnover ≤ EUR 35,000). ATAD 2 reverse-hybrid characterization may apply where partners are resident in jurisdictions that treat the SCSp as opaque, displacing transparency for deduction disallowance purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée - TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for the small-business franchise (exemption); no threshold for non-resident suppliers of B2C e-services (OSS registration from first euro) or for B2B cross-border services subject to reverse charge; EUR 10,000 intra-Community threshold for distance sales and e-services to non-taxable persons
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API clearance or digital stamping regime in force. Luxembourg has no mandatory B2B e-invoicing yet; B2G invoices must be issued as structured e-invoices via the Peppol network (PEPPOL BIS 3.0). Under the EU VAT in the Digital Age package (Council Directive amending Directive 2006/112/EC, adopted 11 March 2025), Luxembourg will transpose mandatory e-invoicing and digital e-reporting for intra-EU B2B supplies by 1 July 2030 and expects domestic B2B e-invoicing obligations from 1 January 2028. Invoices (paper or electronic) must be retained for 6 years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies to export supplies of goods where the customs export declaration (EAAD/MRN) is lodged and physical exit from the EU is evidenced within 90 days (Art. 55 VAT Law and AEDT circulars). B2B remote screen-share/IoT telemetry services to non-EU customers fall outside Luxembourg VAT scope (no Luxembourg VAT, not 'zero-rated' in the strict sense); B2B services to EU customers are reverse-charged in the recipient's jurisdiction, conditional on the customer's valid EU VAT ID; B2C supplies of digital services to EU consumers are taxed where the consumer is established via the VAT OSS scheme (no threshold for non-EU-service suppliers), while B2C supplies to non-EU consumers remain outside Luxembourg VAT. Zero-rating substantiation for software/telemetry services includes contractual IP/user documentation, network logs and payment evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (EAAD) with MRN evidencing EU exit (for goods)
Transport document: Bill of Lading, CMR consignment note, or Air Waybill (signed/dated by carrier)
Commercial invoice in the name of the purchaser stating the export exemption basis
Protocole/inter-party evidence of the exported service scope, licence agreement or remote-access logs (for remote screen-share and IoT telemetry services)
Bank statement/proof of inward payment evidencing consideration received and FX repatriation (inward remittance certificate as issuer-bank certified equivalent)
Valid EU VAT ID of the customer (for reverse-charge B2B services within the EU)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEDT audits export/zero-rating files for up to 6 years; missing or falsified export evidence triggers retroactive clawback of the exemption plus default interest of 0.6% per month and a late-payment surcharge of 10%; intentional misstatements attract a tax increase of up to 50% of the evaded VAT, and fraud (Art. 425/426 General Tax Law) carries criminal fines up to EUR 250,000 and/or imprisonment up to 5 years. The general partner and the SCSp are jointly and severally liable for VAT debts; refund claims are deferred while the export dossier is under verification.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque Centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting within the Eurosystem framework of the European Central Bank (ECB); banking prudential supervision is exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) under the Law of 5 April 1993 on the financial sector.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg applies comprehensive euro-zone convertibility for both current-account and capital-account transactions, implemented through EU primary law (TFEU Article 63 free movement of capital) and national law. The euro is freely convertible; profit remittances, partnership distributions, and the repatriation of invested capital by the SCSp's non-resident limited partners are not subject to exchange-authorisation, licensing, or surrender requirements. The only practical hurdles are (i) statutory AML/CFT and UBO transparency checks (Law of 13 January 2019 on the UBO register), (ii) source-of-funds verification under CSSF Circular 17/650, and (iii) mandatory balance-of-payments statistical reporting of cross-border payment flows routed through Luxembourg banks (generally reported by the bank once a transaction exceeds EUR 12,500). No material convertibility hurdle exists for a remote-screen-share/IoT software business receiving subscription revenue from global customers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender timeline or mandatory conversion ratio applies to export receipts in Luxembourg. Software subscription and licence income is treated as current-account service revenue; proceeds may be retained in EUR or foreign currency without forced repatriation or conversion. The SCSp is required only to record receipts in its statutory books and to facilitate statistical declarations where the payer is a non-resident; the servicing bank automatically captures and files these data with the BCL under the Grand-Ducal balance-of-payments reporting framework. Voluntary conversion of foreign-currency receipts into EUR is unrestricted.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Overall feasibility: Medium. EEA-licensed and appropriately passported Payment Institutions / Electronic Money Institutions (PSD2) are legally usable for operational treasury functions: collecting Stripe/Paddle settlement payouts, making international contractor payments, and executing FX conversions. They are NOT permissible for capital-subscription escrows or long-term reserve deposits, because deposit-taking is statutorily reserved to credit institutions under the Law of 5 April 1993. Offshore non-EEA digital EMIs present material legal, tax-substance, and AML objections for a Luxembourg SCSp and should be avoided for the primary banking relationship.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening is permissible under CSSF Circular 17/650 where the bank applies qualified electronic identification (eIDAS, e.g., LuxTrust) and video-certified identity verification. In practice, tier-1 Luxembourg institutions require at least one senior officer of the General Partner to complete a structured video compliance interview; physical attendance is frequently mandated where no local Luxembourg director exists, where signatories hold non-EU passports not eligible for remote verification, or where the UBO structure involves trusts/nominees. A Luxembourg registered-office provider with domiciliation powers and a GP governed by Luxembourg directors materially reduces the probability of a compulsory in-person visit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-transparent SCSp lacking separate legal personality; bank cannot conclusively identify partnership UBOs
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised partnership deed, certified extract from the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register, UBO register extract under the Law of 13 January 2019, a powers-and-binding-opinion letter confirming that the General Partner alone acts for the SCSp, and a legal opinion from a Luxembourg law firm explaining the SCSp's transparency and the capital-commitment schedule.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident technology founders with remote residence and opaque source of initial capital injection
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Professional source-of-wealth letter, six months of personal and corporate bank statements evidencing legitimate accumulation, audited or accountant-certified financials of prior ventures, payslips or capital-gain documentation, and, for contributions above EUR 1 million, an independent audit attestation or reputable tax-adviser declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Remote screen-sharing and IoT telemetry product perceived as exposing the bank to money-mule or cyber-fraud risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: B2B-only contracting policy and sample subscriber agreements, geo-blocking and sanctions-screening protocol for prohibited jurisdictions, Stripe/Paddle abandonment and chargeback statistics, GDPR and data-protection compliance manual, and the platform's fraud-monitoring documentation demonstrating merchant integrity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Settlement flows arriving from Stripe/Paddle as payment intermediaries rather than from named software customers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Controlled merchant statements from Stripe/Paddle, payout-volume forecast, platform KYC/merchant verification certificates, a legal undertaking that funds derive exclusively from software licensing and not from third-party pass-through transactions, and commitment to attach the SWIFT/TARGET payment reference chain and invoices for every inbound repatriation above EUR 50,000.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contributions from limited partners must be routed via SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR payments up to EUR 100,000 per transaction, or via SWIFT MT103 (with or without cover) for larger sums and non-EUR currencies. The General Partner must issue a payment instruction letter naming the SCSp as beneficiary, quoting the BCL balance-of-payments statistical purpose code applicable to equity-capital/direct-investment remittances, and attaching the subscribed capital schedule from the partnership deed. The receiving bank verifies funds under CSSF Circular 17/650: each contributing limited partner must provide FATCA/CRS self-certification, identification documents, and source-of-funds evidence matching the transacting entity; funds settled from third-party accounts must be accompanied by a formal gift/shareholder-funding declaration acceptable to the bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements and operating disbursements are executed through SEPA Credit Transfer for EU-originated vendor invoices, SEPA Instant for urgent EUR payments below EUR 100,000, and SWIFT MT103 for non-EU counterparties and multi-currency payments; SWIFT gpi tracking is applied for confirmation and compliance screening. For infrastructure and reseller contracts above EUR 250,000, a commercial documentary letter of credit (UCP 600) or bank payment obligation may be established where the counterparty requires payment risk mitigation; otherwise, standard corporate treasury practice is direct MT202/COV interbank settlement with STP payment orders and ISO 20022 pain.008 files.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP) with tenors up to 12 months
FX Swaps combining spot and forward legs for liquidity management
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for hedging structural non-EUR obligations
European-style FX Options (call/put) executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are inapplicable to the euro gateway; NDFs are reserved for illiquid/restricted emerging-market currencies and are not a permissible or necessary instrument for the SCSp's standard EUR/USD exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of Annual Accounts (Depot des comptes annuels) with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Societes (R.C.S.), Luxembourg
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of the financial year end (deadline 31 July for a 31 December year end); no statutory extension for ordinary filers.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or refusal to file attracts administrative fines up to EUR 2,000 per defaulting officer, publication of the default in the RCS extract, and two or more consecutive missed filings may trigger administrative strike-off (radiation) with loss of entity standing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO Register Confirmation / Beneficial Ownership Declaration (Registre des Beneficiaires Effectifs - RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - RBE (Registre des Beneficiaires Effectifs), Luxembourg
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: File within 1 month of any change in beneficial ownership; annual year-end reconciliation must be filed whenever a partnership-interest transfer has occurred; otherwise the RBE record must remain continuously current.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines of EUR 250 to EUR 1,250 per violation under Article 16 of the RBE Law; publication of defaulting entities on the RBE non-compliance register; wilful non-filing may result in personal liability of the managing partner.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Net Wealth Tax Declaration (impot sur la fortune) - only where the SCSp has validly opted for corporate taxation; the default SCSp status is fiscally transparent and not subject to entity-level net wealth tax.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 May following the relevant tax year (electronic filing; calendar year basis).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts a 10% surcharge on the assessed net wealth tax plus 0.6% monthly interest; failure to file enables ex-officio assessment and enforced collection against the SCSp assets; nil returns must nonetheless be filed where the option has been exercised.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit by a reviseur d'entreprises agree applies if the SCSp exceeds at least two of three thresholds for two consecutive financial years: balance-sheet total EUR 4.4 million / net turnover EUR 8.8 million / average annual employees 50; an audit is also required when imposed by the partnership agreement, investor side letters, or a supervisory authority.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Plan Comptable Normalise) under the Law of 19 December 2002 on accounting obligations; IFRS optional for consolidated accounts and required for certain supervised financial vehicles.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: SCSp is a contractual partnership: on any transfer or issue of partnership interests, the RBE declaration must be updated within 1 month; at each annual closing the general partner must verify the UBO waterfall and, where any change occurred, file the amended RBE confirmation before the annual accounts deposition; the RBE maintains a current-at-all-times standard rather than a single annual renewal deadline.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 - 18,000 per annum (only where audit is voluntary or mandated)

approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
